No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I treated the requested value as the largest off-resonant bulk \(d\)-tensor component. These are structure-based estimates; actual SHG values can vary substantially with wavelength, band gap, defects, and phase purity. Structures inferred to be centrosymmetric were assigned \(d=0\).

The main indicators were:

- inversion symmetry, which forbids electric-dipole SHG;
- polar or noncentrosymmetric tetrahedral networks;
- anion polarizability, approximately Te \(>\) Se \(>\) S \(>\) halides;
- Cu/Ag/Hg/Tl and stereochemically active lone-pair cations, which tend to enhance nonlinear response;
- cancellation between differently oriented local coordination units.
